terms.comment: Both nominatives are classical, vallis and vallēs; Lewis & Short and Traupman give vallēs first, and the readers write it.
The same word with a nominative in -ēs, Caesar’s form; Lewis & Short and Traupman give it first.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 206 and p. 401, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-ovidius), checked against the editions named there.

phrases.latin: hoc pecus omne meum est, multae quoque vallibus errant, multās silva tegit, multae stabulantur in antrīs
phrases.english: this whole flock is mine; many more wander in the valleys, many are hidden in the woods, many are penned in caves
